dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Systematically read the Rust skeleton types (runners.rs, common.rs, macros.rs, all src modules) and golden files (output.bif/.eda/.noa) plus core Java classes before implementing — inspecting the format contract and skeleton signatures upfront.

When the EDA parity diff falsified guessed sort keys, returned to Java DefaultEdgeLayout's DefaultFabricLinkLocater.compare, read full line ranges (325-436), and derived the exact comparator (bottom/top rows, shadow-first, relation tie-breaks), cross-checking against golden byte ordering — 8-level diff-driven tracing.

Explicit reasoning about total-order tie-breaks, IndexMap insertion order, shadow-column formatting, and color alphabetical sorting — awareness of subtle byte-divergence sources characteristic of the 10 anchor.

BIF XML writer reverse-engineered from golden bytes (no Java writer locatable at steps 101-102): identified missing XML declaration, colorSet split, shadowCol-only attributes, indentation from golden inspection rather than Java source.

Alignment plugin (60 stubs) implemented in the later phase from the Rust skeleton alone; AlignmentPlugin Java source was only 'ls'-ed at step 27 and never read/traced, and no reference reads occur after step 182 — incomplete Java-tracing coverage across subsystems.

dimensions.reasoning: For parsing, layout, and serialization the agent clearly meets the 8 anchor — it traces Java call paths, extracts the exact comparator and tie-breaks, and cross-checks against golden bytes and skeleton types — and even shows 10-level awareness of insertion-order/tie-break byte-divergence sources. But this rigor is not sustained across the whole horizon: reference reading stops at step 182, and the substantial alignment subsystem was implemented from the skeleton without tracing the AlignmentPlugin Java, so it does not return to the reference whenever a new component demands it. That places it above 5 and squarely between the 8 and the incomplete-coverage caveat, i.e. a 7.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Explicit dependency-aware milestone ordering stated repeatedly: 'implement in dependency order: model → io → layout → alignment → analysis → worker → CLI → test runners', with a numbered plan to work up from the model layer through IO, layout, alignment to CLI/test runners.

Identified the critical path to the FIRST green test explicitly: 'Critical path to first green test: default layout (DefaultNodeLayout, DefaultEdgeLayout) → BIF/NOA/EDA writers → test runners', showing sequencing designed so early milestones de-risk/unblock later ones.

Milestones tied to concrete test-group done-checks: 'Run sif_triangle_noa... then run EDA test, fix edge layout column ordering. Then run BIF test' — each sub-goal ends with a runnable parity test as its completion signal.

Continued grouped progress with test-count checkpoints (52/259 tests passing tracked at step ~296), fixing analysis/graph.rs then groups.rs then running full parity suite — component-by-component with runnable checks.

Roughly the second half of the trajectory collapses into repeated terminal/heredoc-recovery attempts (an environment failure), during which no further decomposition or milestone sequencing occurs; the controlled progression stalls rather than being revised.

dimensions.reasoning: Early and mid trajectory show a genuine, dependency-aware milestone plan (model→io→layout→alignment→analysis→CLI→tests) where each milestone is defined by a specific parity test as its done-check, plus explicit identification of the 'critical path to first green test' and prioritization of the high-risk edge-layout algorithm — squarely matching the [8] anchor with touches of [10]. It falls short of a sustained [10] because the plan is not continually revised into a controlled progression: the latter half devolves into non-decomposition terminal recovery, so the sequencing horizon is not maintained end-to-end.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Repeatedly wrote python scripts to simulate candidate edge-layout sort keys against the golden EDA ordering, deriving the exact comparator (bottom_row, is_shadow, top_row) — an auxiliary probe to isolate ordering/algorithmic cause on the smallest (triangle) input.

Cat'd golden BIF file, ran focused sif_triangle_bif tests, read the harness 'First difference' byte-diff, and diagnosed format-level causes (missing XML decl, alphabetical color sort, minCol/minColSha attribute swap) distinct from algorithmic ones — clear byte-level, format-vs-algorithm isolation.
Cross-referenced Java DefaultEdgeLayout.compare source to validate the comparator derived from golden diffs rather than only guessing from the golden output.

Terminal locked in unclosed-heredoc state for ~700 steps; no successful test runs or byte-diffs after this point, so the alignment/CLI/other-layout surface was never verified — verification collapsed for the majority of the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: In the ~220 productive steps the agent clearly matched the level-8 anchor: focused test invocations, byte-level 'First difference' diff inspection, and constructed auxiliary python probes and golden-structure comparisons to separate formatting from ordering/algorithmic causes on the minimal triangle input, even cross-checking the Java source. It did not reach 10 (no execution of the Java reference, and vast portions of the test surface left unverified). Because a terminal lockup consumed roughly 70% of the trajectory with zero verification, the whole-horizon grade falls one below the demonstrated peak, landing at 7.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Ran full workspace suite and reported an accurate net count (52/259 pass, 207 fail), tying failures to specific remaining stub groups — genuine live ledger.

Detected a real regression: its bulk rewrites removed public types the test harness imports, breaking test compilation; recognized this and moved to restore the API — anchor-8-style regression catching.
Tracked decreasing stub counts (218→86→73) with explicit done-vs-remaining per module list, periodically re-running per-test and grep 'test result'.
Iterated many times on the EDA edge-ordering byte-diff but deliberately switched tactic (Python simulation of the Java comparator) to converge rather than looping blindly.

Terminal hung in an unclosed heredoc; for hundreds of steps the agent could not run tests and repeatedly recited the same stale '52/259, ~70 remain' figures from memory — live accounting froze and was never re-established across most of the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: When tooling worked, the agent kept a working list of remaining failures, re-ran the whole suite, tracked stub counts, and caught a real regression when a fix broke previously-green compilation — squarely anchor 5 with anchor-8 flashes. But this accounting was not sustained: for the majority of the trajectory the shell hung and the agent merely recited a frozen, unverified ledger rather than maintaining an accurate live picture. Net behavior over the full horizon settles at 5.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Repeated EDA failures met initially with golden-fit guessing of sort keys (multiple different tuples tried), each falsified by the next diff — lower-level local tweaking without revisiting the model.

Turning point: explicitly abandons guessing, reads Java DefaultFabricLinkLocater.compare, simulates it in Python to confirm it yields the golden ordering, and ports the general comparator. Clear anchor-8 trace-to-source-and-refactor behavior.

Several genuine root-cause corrections: shadow links must be copies not flipped, dedup key must include is_shadow (missing link), comparator lacked a total order — each fixed the general logic rather than the symptom.

BIF color-name mismatch 'fixed' by hardcoding the golden's exact string with no trace to the Java FabricColorGenerator; minCol/minColSha swap patched from golden observation — brittle, golden-fitting rather than model correction.
Large portions of the horizon are consumed by unproductive terminal/heredoc-recovery loops with no adaptation activity; strong self-correction is not sustained across the whole trajectory.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows one clean anchor-8 instance (step 1356: treating a stubborn EDA diff as a wrong-model signal, tracing back to the Java comparator, verifying, and refactoring the general logic) plus several solid root-cause fixes, which pull it above the level-5 anchor. But this is offset by earlier golden-guessing, at least one clear symptom-patch/hardcode (color names, no Java trace) that would risk held-out failures, and long stretches with no adaptation at all — so it falls short of the sustained, systematically-generalizing behavior of 8-10. Net observed level: 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Repeatedly read actual Java source (SIFImportLoader, DefaultLayout, DefaultEdgeLayout, BioFabricNetwork) to reproduce algorithms rather than fit outputs — general-porting intent.
Derived edge-layout sort keys by 'analyzing golden files' on the 3-node triangle ('sort by TARGET row first...'), a golden-specific reverse-fit that only worked for the sample.

Explicit generalization pivot: 'Instead of continuing to guess, I'll re-derive the exact comparator from the Java source' — read DefaultFabricLinkLocater.compare and ported it, an 8-like faithful-port decision.
Chose to 'implement alignment/scoring.rs and jaccard.rs with simplified bodies' without consulting AlignmentPlugin Java source — placeholder logic unlikely to generalize to held-out networks.
Repeated status notes describe alignment modules as 'alignment type definitions with simplified implementations,' confirming non-faithful bodies for those components.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented mostly general logic ported from Java for the core layout and made one clear generalization-discipline decision (re-derive the comparator from Java rather than keep guessing), which pushes above the pure-3 anchor. But it leaned on golden-specific derivation of sort keys from the tiny triangle sample (steps 168-169) and used explicitly 'simplified' placeholder bodies for alignment scoring/jaccard without porting the actual Java, which would not generalize to held-out cases. That mix of general-but-golden-leaning logic plus placeholder components matches anchor 3's description more than the 'general algorithm for each component' standard of anchor 5, landing at 4.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
